title: Devlens Analysis: Who is hiring in Bangladesh's development sector this week
excerpt: 46 open roles: almost two in five are in Cox's Bazar, international NGOs post half of them, and national NGOs barely appear on job portals.
content:
Every Tuesday, Devlens looks at the numbers behind the sector. This week: the 46 development and humanitarian jobs open on the Devlens jobs board on 10 November 2026. The board lists vacancies from UN agencies, international and national NGOs, donors and research centres, checked against each employer’s own advert. It does not cover every vacancy in Bangladesh, so read these figures as a snapshot of the roles we track, not a census.

Where the jobs are

Almost two in five open roles are in Cox’s Bazar. That is a large share for one district and reflects how much of the sector’s hiring still comes from the Rohingya response, even as its funding falls.

What kind of work

Who is hiring

One employer, the International Rescue Committee, accounts for 15 of the 46 roles, almost all of them in Cox’s Bazar. Only three roles come from national NGOs (BRAC, WAVE Foundation and the Society for Social Service), which is far below their real share of the sector’s workforce. National NGOs rarely use the international job portals we monitor, and often advertise only in Bangla newspapers or on Bdjobs. We are widening our search of those sources.

Who can apply

  • 11 roles are for Bangladeshi nationals only, mostly UN national officer posts and local contracts.
  • 9 roles are consultancies, most of them with UNICEF.
  • 24 roles have no fixed deadline (“open until filled” or “see advert”). Apply early for these: employers can close them without notice.

Deadlines

More than half the roles with a fixed deadline close within a week. Job seekers should check the closing soon list every few days.

What it tells us

  • The humanitarian response still drives hiring, even though aid to Bangladesh is shrinking. Contracts in Cox’s Bazar are often short, many running to the end of December or March.
  • Health is the second biggest area, consistent with the measles and dengue outbreaks and the government’s plan to expand primary healthcare.
  • Finance and operations roles are steady, a reminder that compliance and grant management skills are in demand as donors tighten reporting.
  • Climate, gender and governance roles are scarce on the board, despite the attention these themes get in strategies and at COP31.

How we counted

All open roles listed on the Devlens jobs board on 10 November 2026, after removing expired listings. Employer type is based on the hiring organisation; international NGOs include organisations headquartered abroad such as Plan International, FHI 360, Heifer International, Winrock International and Noora Health. Locations follow the employer’s advert. Employers can send us vacancies to list for free.
